item.title: France Protests Show Europe’s Shift Away From Centrist Politics
item.description: Europe’s centrist parties are losing ground among young people and workers, who are increasingly tempted by populist promises of radical change.

item.title: Student Protesters in France Have a Strange New Slogan. What Does It Mean?
item.description: “Bismillah, c’est les ténèbres” has appeared on signs at recent demonstrations. It doesn’t make much sense (it means, “In the name of God, it’s the darkness”) but is seen as shorthand for a generational divide.

item.title: Robert Kabera, Rwandan Government Critic, Beheaded in Uganda
item.description: The former soldier had been living in exile since 2020, and said in a video posted this month on TikTok that he feared for his life.

item.title: Yemeni City of Taiz Running Out of Essentials as Houthis Close in
item.description: The Iranian-backed Houthi militia has cut road access to Taiz, one of Yemen’s largest cities, besieging it. Officials there warn of an impending humanitarian disaster.

item.title: 178 Years After Banning Slavery, France Scraps ‘Code Noir’ Rules That Governed It
item.description: In a symbolic move, the French Senate approved the repeal of regulations that had remained on the books long after slavery’s abolition.

item.title: Why Zelensky Took the Gloves Off This Time With Trump
item.description: Staying quiet is riskier than speaking up, Ukrainian officials say, as President Trump goes further than ever in prioritizing Russia’s interests.

item.title: UK to Send Fighter Jets to Help Defend Saudi Arabia From Houthi Attacks
item.description: R.A.F. Typhoon fighter jets will be deployed to protect infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, Britain said, after a spike in attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi militia.

item.title: France to Extend Curfews After Calm Night Follows Days of Riots
item.description: The targeted restrictions are part of a state effort to reassert control after the country’s largest riots in years, as those arrested in the chaos face expedited trials.

item.title: Rubio Travels to India to Strengthen Economic Ties Amid Strained U.S. Relations
item.description: The secretary of state will meet with Asia’s richest men in Mumbai as Washington continues negotiations over a trade deal with India.

item.title: A Chef Celebrates Immigrant Flavors in Anti-Migrant South Africa
item.description: A self-taught chef borrows ingredients and ideas from restaurants run by immigrants in South Africa, hoping to help counter rising xenophobia.

item.title: The Mayor of a City in Haiti Warned of a Massacre. No One Listened.
item.description: The mayor of Kenscoff, a town near Haiti’s capital, wrote government officials hundreds of letters to warn of gang threats. Then dozens of people died, and he did, too.

item.title: Hegseth Said to Make Unannounced Visit to Israel for Talks With Netanyahu
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Israel’s defense minister, a week before a pivotal election.

item.title: The A.I. Data Center Backlash Has Reached a Quiet Corner of Rural England
item.description: Plans to build one of Europe’s largest data centers in Devon have been met by strong opposition from residents, as environmental concerns grow.

item.title: Australian Lawmaker Helen Haines Remains in Critical Condition After Car Attack
item.description: Helen Haines, an independent, remained in critical condition after she was struck by a vehicle. A 43-year-old man was charged and will appear in court on Wednesday.

item.title: As Alberta Rejects Canada Separatism, Carney Gets Much of the Credit
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney won over Canada’s most conservative province by promising a pipeline and campaigning hard, defeating its efforts to secede.

item.title: Art Basel Paris Preview Draws Interest Despite Protests
item.description: The Avant-Première preview of the Art Basel Paris fair attracted major collectors despite an escalation of anti-government protests, riots and looting across French cities.

item.title: Nigeria Announces First Case of Ebola in Current Outbreak
item.description: Health officials praised the Nigerian authorities for their transparency in reporting the spread of the virus.

item.title: China Criticizes U.S. Ban on DeepSeek A.I. in Government Systems
item.description: The response came after Homeland Security ordered the removal and exclusion of products developed by the Chinese company.

item.title: Is Putin’s Waiting Game Working?
item.description: Trump’s push for deals and Europe’s political fractures seem to be giving the Russian president the opening he’s been waiting for.

item.title: The British Police Rearrest Two in Connection With Alleged Terror Plot
item.description: The counterterrorism police investigating a threat against an English air base used by U.S. bombers said the two men were working on behalf of Iran.
